questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: determine an unknown concentration from a calibration equation
questions.stem: A calibration line has slope 0.211 and intercept 0.072. An unknown gives a signal of 1.376. What is its concentration from y = mx + b?

options.misconception: multiplies by the slope instead of dividing
adds the intercept instead of subtracting it when solving
ignores the intercept of the calibration line

questions.explanation: Rearranging y equals m x plus b gives x equals y minus b all over m. Subtracting the intercept removes the baseline signal and dividing by the slope converts signal into concentration. The other operations misapply the line equation.
questions.hint: Isolate x from y = mx + b.

questions.learningObjective: determine an unknown concentration from a calibration equation
questions.stem: A calibration line has slope 0.554 and intercept 0.103. An unknown gives a signal of 1.889. What is its concentration from y = mx + b?

options.misconception: ignores the intercept of the calibration line
adds the intercept instead of subtracting it when solving
multiplies by the slope instead of dividing

questions.explanation: Rearranging y equals m x plus b gives x equals y minus b all over m. Subtracting the intercept removes the baseline signal and dividing by the slope converts signal into concentration. The other operations misapply the line equation.
questions.hint: Isolate x from y = mx + b.
